title: tier-2 shipped code: the entry find against DynamicIndexFindEntry (0x1425111a0)

unreachableBranches.why: the equal-path `cmp ebx, r15d; je` at 0x142511265: ebx is mid = (lo+hi)>>1 with lo<hi (the loop test at 0x14251125a), so mid < hi always and the equal exit to the page scan is never taken. The taken path is the expansion that follows.

the pointer-array growth entry `cmp ecx, eax; jne` at 0x142511375 (eax is the 32-slot stack capacity with bit 31 cleared): the not-taken edge needs exactly 32 matching page records, and the growth it enters allocates through the allocator vtable at [segment] (+0x18 alloc, +0x30 free) with a 0x142efe2b0 copy - callees outside the system whose new base pointer cannot be compared byte for byte. Every fixture case keeps matches <= 32 (the probe rejects more), so the taken edge (no grow) is what runs.

the end-of-scan `test [rsp+0x8c], 0x80000000; jne` at 0x1425114f9: the high bit marks the stack pointer array and is set until a growth replaces it, so with no growth the jne is always taken to the cookie check. The fall-through frees the grown array through the allocator vtable at [segment]+0x30, the declared growth gap.

notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/index.rs::find_entry (the byte-view form over the 18-byte entries, the page table and the fresh key state), built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the dynamic_index_find_entry entry. The ledger binds the verdict to index.rs + the probe source + the git revision. SegmentEntries::key_state was refactored onto find_entry (its typed entries and page records become the byte forms), so the shipped path and the tested function are the same code, not a parallel copy; SegmentEntries::find_range remains the typed equal-range view and agrees with the walk on the install tests.

Oracle is DynamicIndexFindEntry at exe 0x1425111a0, measured extent 0x1425111a0..0x142511539 (921 bytes through the ret at 0x142511538; the .pdata root is only 0x1425111a0..0x1425111c4, 0x24 bytes, and the body continues past it, with no tail-jump - the exit is the cookie check through 0x1426c3d40 and the ret), which is the declared coverageWindow. v2b 0x7ff7c72311a0 is computed as 0x7ff7c4d20000 + (0x1425111a0 - 0x140000000) and cross-checked against fn/DynamicIndexDecodeEntries at 0x1425209a0 -> 0x7ff7c72409a0. Signature: (segment *segment, const key[9] *key, key_state *ctx, u32 *out_page, u32 *out_record) -> void (RCX, RDX, R8, R9, then the stack argument). The segment fields are entries base at +0x58, entry count at +0x60, page-table base at +0x68 and page count at +0x70. The key state is the caller-built one from DynamicIndexFindContextInit (0x142520520): found at +0x10, chosen at +0x18, inline interval buffer at +0x28 with its base at +0x128, count at +0x130, capacity 16 at +0x134 - this function does not call that init (its caller DynamicIndexResolveRange at 0x1425115d0 does, on the stack, with the segment's [0] and [8] as the context's allocator and logger words).

The shipped find_entry matched the client operation for operation and needed no correction to the earlier find_range/key_state reading: lo = 0, hi = count, the loop ends at lo == hi, mid is the 32-bit (lo+hi)>>1, memcmp over 9 bytes decides hi = mid / lo = mid+1, equality records mid and expands backward (first eight bytes then the ninth) and forward, and an absent key decodes the empty range at its insertion point. The page scan stops at the first zero stored hash, collects matching 19-byte payloads in page/record order, and returns (page, record) of that zero, (page_count, 21) for a full table and (0, 0) for a zero page count. The decode is the call to DynamicIndexDecodeEntries at 0x1425114a3 with the equal range, the collected payloads and a null contiguous range, decoding the 5-byte big-endian location at +9 and the little-endian u32 size at +14.

Compared channels: one 0x6000-byte blob pointee (segment at 0 with relocs for the entries base, page-table base and the allocator/logger words, the allocator slot at 0x1000, the key state at 0x2000 with relocs for its allocator, logger and interval-base words, the entries at 0x3000, the pages at 0x4000, the disabled logger at 0x5200, the key at 0x5600 and the two out words at 0x5700). The four pointer arguments are u64 arena addresses (0 for a null out word), so the probe writes the out words only when the address is non-null, as the client does. The probe writes back the found byte, the chosen entry, the interval count and the whole physical interval buffer (start and delta only - the client never writes a record's padding, which the fixture keeps uniform).

Coverage gate is 86% over the window's 26 conditional branches (sweep-counted; the earlier 28 was a miscount): the empty-count exit (0x14251121b), the memcmp equal/negative/positive split (0x142511241, 0x142511243) and the walk loop (0x14251125a), the equal-path `je` at 0x142511268 (declared dead above), the backward and forward expansion compares (0x142511275, 0x14251128f, 0x14251129a, 0x1425112a1, 0x1425112ab, 0x1425112bb, 0x1425112c6, 0x1425112ce), the zero-page-count exit (0x14251131b), the zero-hash stop (0x142511344), the three page-key compares (0x14251134f, 0x14251135b, 0x142511368), the first growth-entry compare (0x142511377, taken edge, declared dead above), the growth block's own flag test at 0x1425113df, the two page/record loop backs (0x142511448, 0x142511455), the null out-word exits (0x1425114e0, 0x1425114f5) and the end flag test (0x14251150c, taken edge, declared dead above). Three edges are declared unreachable above. The second growth-entry compare at 0x142511382 (`jbe` at 0x142511380, edx = count+1 against the 32-slot capacity) is NOT declared dead: it is reached only when the compare at 0x142511377 falls through, i.e. on a 33rd match (count == 32), and then it inevitably falls through to the allocator-vtable grow at 0x1425113b2, so with matches capped at 32 it never executes at all (0 observed edges) and cannot satisfy the harness rule that a declared-dead site must have run with exactly one edge observed. It therefore counts as a missed site, like the growth flag test at 0x1425113df which also never runs. The two remaining single-edge sites in the earlier corpus are now both-edge: the forward-expansion `jb` at 0x1425112ce falls through when an equal run extends to the last entry (the declared case with an equal pair at indexes 1-2 of three entries, queried at the pair's key: hi is stepped once to count and the loop back is not taken; the taken edge was already covered by the three equal entries in the middle), and the zero-hash `je` at 0x142511344 is taken by the declared case with a zero stored hash at page 0, record 1 (out words (0, 1)). That leaves 26 - 3 = 23 reachable sites of which 21 have both edges: 21/23 = 91.304%, so the gate is set at 91 (92 would exceed the proved figure). The main session confirms the measured figures when it runs the unit.

allowedImageReads lists the only image data the body and its decode/sink callees read: the stack-cookie global at exe 0x143ac5f40 (v2b 0x7ff7c87e5f40), read by the prologue cookie and the epilogue check; the DynamicIndexEntrySink jump table at exe 0x1425206a8..0x1425206c3 (v2b 0x7ff7c72406a8-0x7ff7c72406c3, the seven dwords for types 1-7, reached through the DecodeEntries call); and the float constant at exe 0x142f7aae4 (v2b 0x7ff7c7c9aae4) the sink's type 4/5 branches load. The memcmp call (0x142efecf0), the DecodeEntries call (0x1425209a0) and the cookie-check call (0x1426c3d40) are code, not data reads.

acknowledgedGaps.why: When the page scan collects a 33rd matching record the client grows its stack pointer array through the allocator vtable at [segment] (+0x18 alloc, +0x30 free) with a 0x142efe2b0 copy - callees outside the system whose new base pointer cannot be compared byte for byte, exactly as fn/DynamicIndexAppendInterval declares for the interval grow. Every fixture case keeps matches <= 32 (the probe rejects more), so the growth block past 0x142511382 never runs.

acknowledgedGaps.what: the interval capacity grow inside the decode
acknowledgedGaps.why: The decode appends through DynamicIndexAppendInterval, whose capacity grow (log 0x1424f8440 + allocator vtable at [ctx]) is the declared gap of fn/DynamicIndexAppendInterval and fn/DynamicIndexDecodeEntries. The fixture keeps decode appends <= 8 against the fresh context's capacity of 16 (the probe rejects more), so that grow never runs.

acknowledgedGaps.what: equal interval starts in one pre-normalize buffer
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client's sort (0x14251ff30) is unstable, so two events with the same start but different deltas can be ordered either way and the tail past the new count is not deterministic; the Rust sort_unstable_by_key may pick the other order. Every fixture case keeps all appended interval starts and ends distinct (the one type-4 case appends a caller-built chosen entry at 0x9000, clear of every other interval), so the sorted order is unique on both sides.

acknowledgedGaps.what: a type-4/5 log call with a live logger
acknowledgedGaps.why: The sink's type 4 and 5 branches call the log function at 0x1424f8440 with the logger at [ctx+0x08]. The fixture's logger has level 0 at its +8, so the call returns after its cookie checks without formatting or emitting anything. A live logger's output is outside the system and is not modelled; the shipped sink likewise has no log stage.

acknowledgedGaps.what: an entry array that is not in non-decreasing key order beyond the declared unsorted cases
acknowledgedGaps.why: The client assumes the segment's entries are sorted (the install's are, with 806 duplicate pairs); the walk is still a deterministic memcmp walk on any byte order and the declared unsorted cases pin two of those walks, but a general unsorted array's insertion point is not a meaningful range. Random cases generate sorted entries.
